Commentary.Commentary: Mehidy Hasan is caught for a quick chat before the run chase. Mehidy says that he is really happy with his performance as he did not do well in the last game. Tells Shakib and spin bowling coach Sohail Khan who advised him to bowl in good areas. Says he just wanted to not get hit for boundaries.

Right! Not a very big score on the board by West Indies again. Bangladesh bowlers have done their job. Time for their batters to finish the job and seal the series with one match left. The visitors, on the other hand, will be once again disappointed with their performance. Can they do something with the ball? Join us for the run chase in a short while.

It is a top bowling performance from Bangladesh. Mustafizur once again provided the breakthrough and after that, the spinners took the matter into their own hands. Mehidy Hasan struck twice in the over to peg West Indies further. Shakib continued his good form and got a wicket in his first over. Apart from Rubel, all the bowlers who bowled got at least one wicket to their name. Mehidy ended up with a 4-fer while Shakib and Mustafizur got two to their name.

After winning the toss, West Indies opted to bat first. They had a poor start as Ambris failed to get going again. Debutant Kjorn Ottley looked good in his short stay but once he got out, it was a dismal show from the others. Ottley got out when the score read 36 in the 13th over. By the end of the 18th over the score read 41 for 5. Bonner along with skipper Jason resisted for a while but they failed to go big. West Indies lost their 8th wicket for 88. It looked like they won't even cross 100 but Powell first with Joseph and then with Hosein added valuable runs to take the team close to 150. He eventually got out on 41 and was the last Windies wicket to depart.

Another sorry show for the West Indies with the bat. They never looked to get going in this innings and have been rolled over by the hosts for a low score again. The total would've been a lot smaller if not for Powell's handy innings and his partnerships with Joseph and Akeal. However, credit to the Bangladeshi bowlers but they were helped by some ordinary batting from the visitors.

So he bowls it slightly shorter and quicker outside off. Powell comes down the track and looks to hit him down the track. The West Indies batter misses. Mushfiqur takes a good take behind the stump and does the rest.  WEST INDIES BOWLED OUT FOR 148!

Right! It is time for the action in the middle. Both the umpires stride out first. The Bangladeshi players make their way out in the middle as well. Sunil Ambris anddebutant Kjorn Ottley are the openers for West Indies. Mustafizur Rahman will start with the ball for Bangladesh. Before the action, the players from both the sides take the knee in support of the BLM movement. Play says the umpire. Here we go...

Tamim Iqbal, the Bangladeshi skipper, says that he was pleased with the team's performance overall. Says the seamers and spinners did well in the last game. Feel batting was tough in the last game. Tells he was anyway looking to bowl first. Informs they are unchanged from the last game.

West Indies skipper, Jason Mohammed, tells that it looks like a pretty good wicket and that's why they want to bat first. Wants to put on a good score and then restrict the opposition. Informs one change in the team as Chemar Holder makes way for Kjorn Ottley.

Pitch report - Anjum Chopra is in with the pitch report. Tells that the surface offers a lot for the batters. Feels spinners from both the teams did really well. Informs the weather is all good. Says win the toss and bat first is what she will prefer.

Bangladesh (Unchanged Playing XI) - Tamim Iqbal (C), Liton Das, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Shakib Al Hasan, Mushfiqur Rahim (WK), Soumya Sarkar, Mahmudullah, Mehidy Hasan, Hasan Mahmud, Rubel Hossain, Mustafizur Rahman.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Sunil Ambris, Joshua Da Silva (WK), Andre McCarthy, Nkrumah Bonner, Jason Mohammed (C), Rovman Powell, Kyle Mayers, Akeal Hosein, Raymon Reifer, Alzarri Joseph, Kjorn Ottley (IN FOR CHEMAR HOLDER).
Toss - Time for the flip of the coin. Both the captains are out in the middle. Up goes the coin and it lands in favor of West Indies. THEY WILL BAT FIRST.

Hello and welcome to the 2nd game of the 3-match ODI series between Bangladesh and West Indies. In the first game of the series, the hosts thrashed the visitors and strolled to victory. It was their bowlers who set up the victory by restricting the depleted West Indies side to a low score. Then their batters without taking much risk took the team over the line. Shakib al Hasan shone with the ball while skipper Tamim Iqbal showed good batting form. Debutant Hasan Mahmud too had a great game. So, how will things pan out in this game? Will West Indies be able to turn things around or will Bangladesh continue to dominate? We will find out answers to all these soon. Stay with us for the toss and team updates.
